verdict_reason: The token-endpoint fix works and is tested, but the unavailable-status rule now has two homes and the class name no longer says what it configures.

todos.issue: The rule that 502, 503 and 504 mean a dependency is unavailable now has two homes, both added by this PR: 'if (ex.status() == 502 || ex.status() == 503 || ex.status() == 504)' at MdmClientInterceptor.java:64 and 'case 502, 503, 504' at MdmErrorDecoder.java:15. A change to one (adding 500, say) leaves the MDM and token paths classifying the same status differently. The token path is also a second mechanism beside the error decoder, and it repeats 'throw new TokenEndpointUnavailableException("Token endpoint unavailable", ex)' at lines 62 and 65.
todos.fix: Must: one place owns which statuses mean unavailable, the MDM and token paths both use it, and the token path has one throw of TokenEndpointUnavailableException. One way: give TradeApiClient its own ErrorDecoder built on a shared status check, leaving only the RetryableException catch in getToken.

todos.issue: This PR adds '@Bean public ErrorDecoder mdmErrorDecoder()' to a class called MdmClientInterceptor. The class is not an interceptor: it is the Feign configuration for the MDM client ('configuration = MdmClientInterceptor.class' at MdmClient.java:15), and it now supplies error decoding too. A reader looking for how MDM errors are decoded would not open a class in the interceptor package with this name.
todos.fix: Must: the class that configures the MDM Feign client has a name and package that say so, and covers both beans it supplies. One way: rename it MdmClientConfiguration, move it out of the interceptor package, and update MdmClient and the test to match.
